title: Allocative priority preemption causes metering gap in multi-tenant routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: We observed systematic under-counting of usage for low-priority tenants when the allocative priority preemption policy is active. Symptoms surface as intermittent billing shortfalls and quotas not decrementing after requests are preempted and re-routed to fallback paths. This affects per-key and per-route metering for multi-tenant traffic during congestion windows.
reproduction_steps: 1) Enable allocative priority preemption in the routing policy for a test shard
2) Seed traffic from two tenants A (high-priority) and B (low-priority) with overlapping API keys and shared route alias
3) Saturate the shard so the preemption code evicts B's in-flight requests in favor of A
4) Observe that evicted requests for B are retried via fallback route (route_fallback_v2) and return success
5) Compare meter counts and billing events: requests that were evicted then retried do not increment B's per-route token meter in billing pipeline

investigation_notes: Initial triage found the preemption path correctly signals the reroute but does not attach the original enqueued attribution headers used by the metering pipeline

The fastpath code that serializes request metadata for the billing queue strips tenant/context when eviction is detected to avoid blocking; this optimization predates allocative preemption and assumed no reroute would occur
Telemetry shows a spike in 'origin-mapper-miss' events coincident with preemption windows; correlates with increased use of route_fallback_v2
A local repro harness recreates the missing-attribution behavior with synthetic load and confirms the aggregator drops events lacking original attribution tags
root_cause: When allocative preemption evicts a low-priority request, the preemption fastpath intentionally avoids copying the full attribution envelope to reduce latency. If the request is immediately retried/rewritten to a fallback route, the retry only carries the new route context. The billing/metering pipeline expects a persisted original attribution header (x-origin-tenant/x-origin-key/x-origin-route) and drops or marks the event as UNKNOWN when absent, causing undercounting.
mitigation_workaround: Short-term mitigation: revert allocative preemption rollout on affected shards or disable reroute-to-fallback behavior for preempted requests. We deployed a cluster flag (preempt_attach_attrib=false) to two canary shards which restored correct metering for affected tenants.
proposed_fix: 1) Ensure preemption fastpath copies minimal attribution envelope (tenant ID, API key id, original route alias) into the retry envelope before reroute. 2) Add end-to-end unit tests for preempt+reroute attribution. 3) Update billing aggregator to tolerate/repair missing attributes by consulting recent eviction logs as a fallback reconciliation path.
test_plan: Unit tests: preemption path attaches x-origin-* headers to rerouted requests
Integration tests: synthetic multi-tenant load reproducing eviction then retry and asserting billing increments
E2E canary: deploy fix to 5% of shards with synthetic traffic and monitor 'origin-mapper-miss' and per-tenant token deltas
Load test: validate no measurable latency regression in preemption fastpath under 95th percentile
rollout_plan: 1) Merge fix behind feature flag preempt_attach_attrib (PR #1234)
2) Deploy to internal canaries (dev cluster) and run integration suite
3) Roll to 5% production shards for 24 hours and monitor billing deltas and latency
4) If stable, 50% for 6 hours, then full rollout
5) Post-rollout: run reconciliation job to backfill missed billing for window between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-05
followups: Add metric: preempt_reroute_with_missing_attrib (counter) and alert if > 1/min for >5m
Backfill job: one-off aggregator job to inspect eviction logs and synthesize missing billing events for affected tenants
Design: revisit performance trade-off that omitted attribution in fastpath and propose compact envelope format to avoid regressions
Docs: update runbook for preemption incidents to include billing validation steps
